author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold a given specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page.
acceptance_criteria: opening /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name
each specialty lists the veterinarians holding it, by first name then last name
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian under it (edge case 1; provisional narrow reading, see Open Questions)
every specialty appears on one page, with no paging
specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
the page's own wording carries no hard-coded text and is present in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002); the specialty name itself is shown as stored, not translated
the page carries the same navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory as every other page (REQ-SYS-001)
non_goals: a navigation entry, menu item, or link to the page from anywhere in the system - reachable by its address alone; a follow-up request may add an entry point
managing veterinarians or specialties through the application - NG-2 is unchanged by this slice
searching or filtering the specialty list - NG-9 is unchanged
a machine-readable representation of the specialty list
notes: file_targets are best-effort; the design stage may place the new page outside the vet package. The eleven message bundles all need the page's labels under REQ-LANG-002. All three seeded specialties are currently held by a veterinarian, so the unheld-specialty case needs test-local data - do not extend the production seed data for it. Edge case 1 (an unheld specialty still renders) is the narrowest reading of 'every specialty the clinic knows' and is recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md; no product answer is available during this slice. No Non-Goals row was changed, so no scope_overrides apply.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the inverse projection of the veterinarian directory and sits in the existing vet feature package. Every element reuses an in-force pattern: a Spring Data lookup repository ordered by name (precedent: PetTypeRepository), a @Controller serving one GET route and one Thymeleaf view (precedent: VetController, WelcomeController), and the shared layout fragment. The one adjustment is a package-private projection type that performs the specialty-to-holders inversion outside the controller, adopted from the Pattern Catalog's 'Available, not currently used' list, which admits adoption without an ADR. No new module, no new dependency, no schema change, no ADR. No durable-memory writes: the Contracts rows describe current state and land at doc-sync time, after the code exists.
integration_points: Route GET /specialties.html renders view vets/specialtyList; the vet package gains a second controller rather than a second method on VetController, so @WebMvcTest can load it alone

The association is unidirectional: Vet.specialties is a @ManyToMany with no inverse on Specialty. The inversion is therefore driven from the vet side (vetRepository.findAll(), whose EAGER fetch makes specialties readable with spring.jpa.open-in-view disabled), while SpecialtyRepository supplies the full specialty set so a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed

SpecialtyRepository extends the narrow Repository<Specialty, Integer> marker declaring one read method with @Transactional(readOnly = true), following VetRepository rather than PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository, which would expose write methods this read-only page must not carry

Ordering: specialties by stored name in the query (ORDER BY, as PetTypeRepository does); holders sorted in SpecialtyListing by the same key the page displays - first name then last name - which is the narrowest reading of acceptance criterion 2 and satisfies the stable-order criterion

patterns.description: lookup-list repository returning rows in name order via an explicit @Query; SpecialtyRepository mirrors it, with VetRepository's narrower Repository base
read-only @GetMapping that loads, builds a model attribute, and returns a view name; SpecialtyController is the same shape minus the pagination helper
page template replacing into the shared layout fragment and rendering names as firstName + ' ' + lastName, all wording through #{} keys

Pattern Catalog, Available-not-currently-used: the inversion is adopted as a stateless read-model type, not added to the controller, since the catalog states a new rule in a controller is a fresh violation

risks.risk: Annotating the specialty read @Cacheable("vets") would collide with VetRepository.findAll(): both are no-arg reads keyed SimpleKey.EMPTY in one cache, so a Collection<Vet> would be returned to a Collection<Specialty> caller
risks.mitigation: leave the specialty read uncached. CacheConfiguration is untouched, and Open Question 5 (no vet cache eviction) is not widened. Reusing the already-cached vetRepository.findAll() for holders is free and safe

risks.risk: New message keys would have to be added to ten bundles, and a missing one fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest
risks.mitigation: the page needs no new key: specialties, vets, name, and none already exist in every bundle. Prefer them. Any distinct wording costs ten files and must be added to all of them except messages_en.properties, which the sync test skips

risks.risk: The page is unpaged by requirement, so its size grows with specialties times holders
risks.mitigation: accepted - no paging is an explicit acceptance criterion and the seeded set is three specialties. Not a defect to fix in this slice

risks.risk: A mirror of the Vets serialization wrapper or a second machine-readable /specialties route would replicate a Known Defect
risks.mitigation: out of scope by the slice's own non-goals; build the HTML route only

notes: Navigation, confirmed against the templates: REQ-SYS-001 is satisfied by using the shared layout, and no Specialties nav item is forced. The nav list in fragments/layout.html is hard-coded (home, find owners, vets, error) and the layout's menu parameter only selects which existing item is highlighted; nothing is generated from a page registry. Reading 'carries the same navigation as every other page' as 'uses the standard layout' is therefore correct, and the slice's no-entry-point non-goal holds with no scope tension. Pass an unmatched key ('specialties') so nothing is highlighted - passing 'vets' would tell the reader they are on the veterinarian directory. Every other template passes a matching key, so this is the first unmatched one; it is inert by construction. Open product question taken at its narrowest: an unheld specialty is listed with the existing #{none} wording under it, matching how vetList.html renders a veterinarian holding no specialty. No product answer was sought. Security: the route adds read-only exposure of data the veterinarian directory already publishes, takes no request parameter and binds no form, so no mass-assignment binder list applies and no request-derived value composes a query or path. Data access stays on derived or parameterized queries; Thymeleaf escaping stays on. Nothing worsens the baseline in security-principles Realization. Reliability: no specialties renders an empty table, an unheld specialty renders none, and a datasource failure falls through to the existing error page - no new blocking call, no long-running work. Testing: put the acceptance criteria for ordering, omission of a veterinarian holding no specialty, and the unheld specialty on SpecialtyListingTests, built from real Vet and Specialty objects with no mock, which is also where the test-local unheld specialty lives - db/h2/data.sql is not touched. SpecialtyControllerTests covers route, view name, and model attribute through MockMvc; prefer a hand-written stub repository over @MockitoBean per CLAUDE.md, falling back to @MockitoBean only if @WebMvcTest wiring makes the stub awkward. The prd-entry's REQ-LANG-002 criterion needs no new test: I18nPropertiesSyncTest walks src/main and picks up the new template automatically. The prd-entry's file_targets, flagged best-effort, put the tests on VetControllerTests; the split above supersedes that placement, and its six test names carry over unchanged. Type names are provisional in shape, not in constraint: the inversion and the holder ordering must live in a package-private, web-free type that is unit-testable without MockMvc. No IntelliJ oracle is connected in this run; the claims above rest on full reads of the named files, which is the weaker basis for symbol resolution.

author: feature-implementer
summary: Read-only specialty directory at GET /specialties.html. SpecialtyListing (package-private, immutable read model) inverts vets onto specialties, matching by specialty id because the two reads run in separate transactions and Specialty has no value equality; holders sort by first name then last name. SpecialtyRepository extends the narrow Repository<Specialty, Integer> marker with one ordered read query, uncached to avoid the SimpleKey.EMPTY collision with @Cacheable("vets"). SpecialtyController serves the page into templates/vets/specialtyList.html via the shared layout with the unmatched menu key 'specialties'. Nine new tests: SpecialtyListingTests (5, real Vet/Specialty objects, no mocks, test-local unheld specialty) and SpecialtyControllerTests (4, MockMvc over hand-written stub repositories, asserting route, view, model attribute and rendered content). No nav entry, no inbound link, no new message keys, db/h2/data.sql untouched, no config change.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties carries a static JPQL literal with no parameters and no request-derived value; sweep of the vet package found no createQuery, nativeQuery, or string-concatenated query text. Marked @Transactional(readOnly = true).

Cross-site scripting: specialtyList.html renders every value through th:text (specialty.name, and the holder first/last name concatenation), so Thymeleaf default escaping applies. Swept templates/vets/ for th:utext, th:inline, and inline script blocks - none present. The pattern matches the existing vetList.html rendering exactly.

No write path introduced: SpecialtyRepository extends the narrow Repository<Specialty, Integer> marker and declares one read method, so no CRUD write is inherited. SpecialtyController exposes @GetMapping only; sweep for PostMapping/PutMapping/DeleteMapping and save/delete calls across the new sources returned nothing. The page is read-only as the requirement states.

Mass assignment and identifier tampering: the handler binds no request-derived value at all - no @ModelAttribute, @RequestParam, or @PathVariable - so there is no binder surface to disallow ids on. Specialty ids used by SpecialtyListing.holdscome from the datastore, never from the caller.

Widening the exposed surface: GET /specialties.html is unauthenticated, which matches the recorded baseline in system-design.md Security Context (no authentication or authorization anywhere; pre-existing absences are not findings). It exposes veterinarian first/last names and specialty names - exactly the data /vets.html already publishes to the same anonymous caller - so it adds no new data class and leaves the application no weaker than baseline. No actuator or management exposure change.
Path traversal and resource resolution: the view name vets/specialtyList and the layout fragment key specialties are compile-time constants, not caller input.
Secrets and error output: no credential, token, key, or connection string in the diff; no new exception message or logging statement, so nothing new reaches the error page.
Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set and no dependency was added, so the four dependency checks do not apply. No new transitive surface to check against the NVD for this pass.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyListing.holds() is documented and implemented to match holders by Specialty id rather than object identity, specifically because specialties and vets are read in separate transactions and arrive as distinct instances of the same row. Every test in this file (and the stub repositories in SpecialtyControllerTests) passes the exact same Specialty instance (e.g. the RADIOLOGY constant) both into the specialties list and into vet.addSpecialty(...). Reference-equality matching would pass every one of these tests just as well as id-based matching does, so the suite does not actually pin the id-matching decision the implementer flagged as load-bearing. A regression that swapped Integer.equals(id) for a raw == or object-equals check on Specialty would not be caught.
findings.fix: Add a case (in theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachHolderByFirstAndLastName or a new test) that constructs two distinct Specialty instances sharing the same id but different object references — e.g. one used in the specialties list, a second (separately-constructed, same id) instance added to the vet — and asserts the vet is still listed as a holder. This is the scenario the separate-transaction reasoning in SpecialtyListing.holds() exists to handle, and it should be the one the test suite actually exercises.

findings.description: The class Javadoc asserts this test needs no @DisabledInAotMode, unlike VetControllerTests/PetControllerTests/OwnerControllerTests/VisitControllerTests in the same and sibling packages, because it uses hand-written @Bean stubs via @Import rather than @MockitoBean. The reasoning is plausible (AOT context processing is documented to be incompatible with MockitoBean's bean overriding) and ./gradlew test passes, but no AOT-mode test run (-Dspring.aot.enabled=true or an AOT smoke build) was exercised in this review to confirm the omission is actually safe rather than merely untested in the mode it claims to be fine under.

answer: Question 1: no doc-sync pass is scheduled, and none would have been. doc-sync is a manually invoked skill, not a routed pipeline stage - no routing condition and no branch of handoff.py route dispatches it, so nothing between here and merge would have added the rows. My line-4 design-block deferred them on a condition ('after the code exists') that is now met with no later hop to honor it; that deferral was wrong on its own terms. The document names no literal route for any controller - the VetController, WelcomeController, and CrashController rows all describe routes behaviorally ('a second route', 'a fixed route'), and Security Context does the same. Its own header rule states source is authoritative for constant values and forbids transcribing literals. One correction to the supporting point you were given: the view-name convention at system-design.md:70 is about view names - the string vets/specialtyList - not about URLs. The instinct to keep the address out of my document is right, but the reason is duplication of a source literal, not privacy - so 'it is a private routing detail' is not a reason to strike it from yours. Where it lives is your call, and I make no claim on it. From the design side there is no competing home, and nothing I wrote contradicts the PRD carrying it.
